extracted_by: hand, T-0294 — the Democrat read, December 1834
note: Vol. II No. 2. Every column of this issue but three is Vision-set, and page 3 is nevertheless the hardest reading of the month: its columns alternate two physical columns line by line for their whole length, so the town's own notices survive as half-lines woven through the legislature's proceedings and a column of reprinted miscellany. The issue's own contribution is a public one — the metes and bounds of School District Number One and the meeting called to act on them at the Mansion House on 16 December. NO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST OF ANY OFFICE STANDS IN THIS ISSUE.

claims.normalized: [A meeting] of the citizens of School Dis[trict Number One] will be held at the [Mansion House on Tuesda]y the 16th day [of December …] — [beginning at …] and[?] south along Willis[ ... to the north west] corner of Block No. 101, in [… thence to the Chicago riv]er, thence south along said riv[er … thence east to the south line?] of said section 16, [… thence east along the south line] of said section to Lake Mich[igan,] thence [nor]th along the Lake shore to [… thence west … to] the place of beginning, [and thence] north to the Chicago river […] is or shall be constituted, known [and descr]ibed as School Distric[t] N[u]mber [One].
claims.notes: THE TOWN'S FIRST SCHOOL DISTRICT IS BOUNDED IN PRINT, AND THE BOUNDS RUN ON REAL GROUND. Willis, block 101, section 16, the Chicago river and the Lake shore are all features this reconstruction already carries, so the description is a closed circuit that could in principle be walked; what stops it being drawn today is the transcription and not the source. THIS IS THE WORST-CUT PASSAGE OF THE MONTH: the notice is woven line by line through a Winnebago-massacre despatch and a chancery order, and better than half of every line is gone with the column edge, so the quote is fifteen surviving lines out of a range of fifty-four and the normalized reading is a skeleton with [ ] at every joint. Nothing is supplied that the fragments do not carry: the compass words that survive are kept, the ones that do not are marked absent. The MEETING is the part that is certain — citizens of the district, at the Mansion House, on the 16th — and it dates the district's organisation to December 1834. The page images would recover the rest of the boundary in one pass; that is worth a ticket and this run files one.

claims.normalized: H. C. BENNETT[,] [ATTORNEY] AND COUNSELLOR AT LA[W,] [and So]licitor in Chancer[y]. [Office fir]st door north from the Tremont [House, o]n Dearborn-street.
claims.notes: A SECOND DOCUMENTED FRONTAGE ON THE SAME FEW FEET OF DEARBORN STREET. Andrews & Eells are one door north of the Tremont House (1834-12-03 c016) and Bennett is FIRST door north of it on Dearborn — so the two are neighbours, or the same door, and the paper does not say which. Both are documented and neither is adjusted to accommodate the other. The 1834-12-24 printing of this same advertisement (page 3 column 4) sets the two halves in the other order — “[Tremont] House, on Dearborn street” — and carries the copy date, 3 December 1834, which is why the trade and the street are read with confidence even though this column is cut to a third of its width.

claims.notes: STOCK IS STILL RUNNING LOOSE AND BEING PENNED FIVE MILES SOUTH-WEST OF THE TOWN AT THE END OF NOVEMBER. This is the second Wentworth in the same month's paper and they are not assumed to be one man: E. Wentworth keeps a public house eighteen miles south of Chicago on the Ottawa road (c005 below), and E. Wentworth, Jr. pens strays five miles south-west. Same surname, and the Jr. is printed, so the gazetteer keys them apart and no merge rule is written — the identity policy's refusal to join a surname across different initials is exactly the guard that should hold here.

claims.notes: A STORE ON SOUTH WATER STREET NEAR THE BRIDGE, AND NOBODY IS MINTED FROM IT, BECAUSE THE NAME IS GONE. The advertiser's signature falls in the half of the physical column the segmenter cut away and no other printing in the month carries it; so this claim records a documented FRONTAGE — near the bridge, on Water street, carrying dry goods, hardware, potash kettles and hollow ware — and mints no business, exactly as the out-of-county letter lists are recorded and not minted. It is NOT assumed to be A. Garrett's store, which takes a store “in South-Water street, [near the] bridge” a week later (1834-12-17 c001) and could be this one or its neighbour; the two are kept apart until a witness joins them.

claims.notes: THE OFFSET THE GAZETTEER WAS MISSING. Clark, Filer & Co. already stand in the gazetteer anchored on “the corner of Randolph st.” with no distance; this printing carries the distance — some number of doors EAST of that corner, on South Water street — and 1834-12-17 page 4 column 1 sets the same clause as “doors east of th[e corner]”. The numeral itself is cut in every December printing: 1834-12-03 reads it as a stray “4”, this one as “bre”, which is three with its t gone. Three is therefore the reading and it is bracketed, because one OCR fragment is not a measurement. The firm's name is taken from the 1834-12-03 printing (page 4 column 1, “CLARK, F[ILER] & Co.”), which this column loses.

claims.normalized: PUBL[IC HOUSE.] E. WE[NTWORTH] [H]AS opened a T[AVERN] 18 [mi]les Sout[h of Chicago, on the road] leading t[o Ottawa. … His table will] be furnish[ed with the best the coun]try afford[s, and … those who] give him [a call … He keeps] on hand [COR]N and [OATS].
claims.notes: EIGHTEEN MILES, AND THIS PRINTING IS WHERE THE NUMBER IS LEGIBLE. The gazetteer carries three separate Wentworth tavern entries from earlier reads — on Flag Creek, on the road to Ottawa, and one with no placement at all — and none of them states the distance. Here it sets as “18 talles Sout”, and 1834-12-17 page 4 column 1 as “1d reiles South of C”, both reading eighteen; 1834-12-03 loses the digits entirely. Eighteen miles south of Chicago on the Ottawa road puts the house well beyond the modelled town and outside the scene, which is exactly why it is worth recording: it fixes the road's stages, and the road is a thing the reconstruction has to point somewhere.

claims.normalized: Blacksmithin[g Business.] MATTHIAS MA[SON] CAR[R]IES on tha[t business in its] various branches, on [… where … all kinds of Work is done on the] … [most liberal terms.]
claims.notes: THE STREET IS CUT AWAY IN ALL FOUR PRINTINGS, AND A FRAGMENT THAT WOULD PLACE HIM BELONGS TO SOMEBODY ELSE. Every December setting of this advertisement ends the sentence at “various branches, on ” and loses the word after it. In the same segmenter column, four to six lines away, stands the fragment “[oppo]site the Tremont Hous[e]” — and it is NOT taken as Mason's, because the lines it sits among are a dry-goods list (English flannels, sattinets, muslins, ginghams, calicoes, merinos) belonging to the OTHER physical column woven into this one, and because assigning a placement across an interleave is precisely the mistake this schema's `interleaved` flag exists to stop. So Mason is minted with placement `none` and the question — whose “opposite the Tremont House” is it — is filed as a ticket by this run. The copy date printed under the advertisement, Nov. 26, 1833, is shared with the dry-goods column and is for that reason not recorded as his.

Three tailoring houses want journeymen in this one month (see 1834-12-03 c005, S. Lincoln); no placement is added here, the Tremont House anchor being carried by the other claim.

claims.notes: THE THIRD FRONTAGE IN THE ROW. T-0313 read this shop in April 1834 as an unattributed “boot and shoe shop next door to P. Cohen's store”; the December printings give the proprietor's name — L. W. MONTGOMERY, legible at 1834-12-03 page 4 column 1 — and the copy date, 15 December 1833, which makes it one of the oldest continuously advertised storefronts in the corpus. Cohen's own advertisement in this month places HIM next door below Newberry and Dole's store house on south water street (1834-12-03 c002), so the chain Newberry & Dole → Cohen → Montgomery is documented end to end, on one street, by two advertisements that do not mention each other. The street on this claim is inherited from Cohen's and is stated as such rather than read off this notice, which prints none.

claims.notes: A FOURTH BUSINESS HUNG OFF NEWBERRY & DOLE'S, WHICH MAKES THAT STORE HOUSE THE MOST USED ANCHOR IN THE CORPUS. Cohen is next door below it, Montgomery next door to Cohen, J. B. Brown's Dearborn-street grocery cites it, and the Chicago Bakery stands a few doors from it on South Water street. The gazetteer carries both a `chicago_bakery` and a `d_graves` keyed apart on the same trade and the same anchor, which is T-0304's firm-merge problem in miniature; this claim does not merge them, it records the printing. The relation word — whether the bakery is above or below the store — is cut away in all four December settings.
